thread:
alex: Quick design q — inline errors vs a top summary for the form validation pattern on the Billing > Payment method flow? I'm weighing noise vs discoverability.
marie: Leaning inline for obvious fields (card number, expiry). Summary at top only when there are multiple errors or hidden fields that failed server-side.
sam: Agree on inline for visible fields. For accessibility though, we should always have an error summary with focus management so screen readers get a single entry point.
jordan: +1 to accessibility requirement. Also: how do we show required markers? Asterisk only? text 'Required'? Both?
emily: Prefer visible "Required" label for clarity on complex forms. Asterisk can be ambiguous without legend. But for compact lists (like a table of quick settings) maybe a single legend works.
alex: Good points. For destructive actions (delete saved card) do we want typed confirmation ("type DELETE") or simple confirm modal? My gut: typed confirmation for multi-card bulk deletes, simple modal for single card.
marie: Exactly — typed confirmation adds friction but prevents catastrophic mistakes on bulk. For single-item deletes, use a modal with clear consequences and a secondary destructive button.
sam: Accessibility nits: ensure confirm modals trap focus, have proper role="dialog" and aria-labelledby, and the typed-confirm input should have aria-describedby explaining why.
jordan: Also ensure inline error messages are programmatically associated with inputs (aria-invalid + aria-describedby -> error id). If we do an error summary, link each bullet to the field anchor with a fragment id.
emily: UX copy suggestion for summary: "We couldn't save — please fix the following issues:" then bullets. Inline: short, action-oriented copy like "Card number is invalid" not just "Invalid".
alex: What about timing? Show inline errors as user types or only on blur/submit? Realtime validation helps, but can be noisy.
marie: For fields like card number, realtime as they type (with len checks) is helpful. For larger textareas (notes), validate on blur/submit.
sam: Implementation note for devs: put error summary at top with id="form-error-summary". On submit failure, focus(document.getElementById('form-error-summary')). Also set role="alert" or use aria-live="assertive" for dynamic errors.
alex: Could someone draft a small spec with these rules and copy examples? I'll own the follow-up.
jordan: I can draft the spec. Quick checklist I'll include:
- Inline errors for visible fields; short copy
- Error summary for submit/server errors and for screen readers
- Focus management to summary on submit failure
- Programmatic linking from summary bullets to fields
- Required state: explicit "Required" for complex forms, asterisk + legend for compact UIs
- Destructive actions: typed confirm for bulk, modal for single
- Accessibility: aria-invalid, aria-describedby, role=dialog, focus trap
emily: Thanks — also add a note about animations: avoid removing focus or jumping content; smooth scroll to error if field is offscreen.
design-bot: Reminder: design review scheduled Fri 10am. Jordan to add PR with spec before Thu EOD. :calendar:
alex: Perfect. Jordan, ping here when you add the doc so we can quickly review before the meeting. :thumbsup:
marie: small UX nit: secondary copy for destructive modal button should be explicit e.g., "Remove card" instead of just "Delete" so it reads in context.
sam: And include a11y tests in the ticket — NVDA/VoiceOver smoke tests for the 3 flows.
jordan: Will do. Draft by EOD Thu and link in this thread.
alex: Thanks all. Short and actionable — exactly what we need.
